title: A Thorn for the Ember
premise: Lena Hartwell has kept the Thornfell gate sealed for twenty years, trading silence with smugglers for the freedom to forget what he sealed behind it. When a boy arrives speaking the Old Tongue of the vanished Emberfolk, Lena learns the covenant he helped break is failing, and the long winter is the realms themselves dying. Hunted by the Crown's inquisitors and the smugglers who want the gate open for their own reasons, Lena must carry the boy to the covenant-stone and speak a truth he has hidden for two decades. He renews the covenant at the cost of his own memories of the gate, and the boy's people, thought extinct, return through the thaw.
about_author: Rosalind Underhill is the pen name of a former cartographer's assistant who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. Her work is known for landscapes that behave like characters and for heroes who would rather stay home.

chapters.title: The Boy at the Door
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A snow-blind child arrives at the gatehouse speaking the Old Tongue, and the ward-stones flare for the first time in twenty years. Lena hides the boy from the first smuggler caravan of the season, lying to men he considers family. Emotional beat: the dread of a quiet life ending, and the first flicker of protectiveness he thought he'd buried.

chapters.title: What the Smugglers Carry
chapters.summary: Alternating Lena's POV with the boy's fragmented memories. The smugglers are smuggling inquisitors, Crown agents hunting Emberfolk survivors, and Lena realizes his old allies sold the road. Fleeing through the high passes, the boy's dreams reveal the covenant-stone lies beyond the gate Lena sealed. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into betrayal, and the choice between his found family and the truth.

chapters.title: The Long Winter's Edge
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, hunted across the frozen Thornfell. The inquisitor captain offers Lena a bargain: the boy in exchange for his old crimes erased. The boy, weakening as the winter deepens, forgives Lena for what he did to the Emberfolk, and forgiveness cuts worse than the cold. Emotional beat: guilt confronted, and the decision that justice outside the law means answering to it yourself.

chapters.title: A Thorn for the Ember
chapters.summary: Lena's POV at the climax. He opens the gate, turns on the inquisitors with the smugglers he can still reach, and speaks his confession into the covenant-stone, offering his memories as the thorn-price. The stone accepts, the winter breaks, and Emberfolk step through into the thaw. Emotional beat: sacrifice transformed into belonging, as the boy chooses to stay with Lena, who no longer remembers why he was ever afraid.
